newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada pledges to send more troops to Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Canada pledges to send more troops to Bosnia.

text.p: Canada offered on Wednesday to increase its contribution to international forces in Bosnia by about 200 troops.
Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy and Defense Minister Doug Young said in a statement that Canada was offering to boost its presence to about 1,200 troops from the current 1,000.
"Canada's involvement in NATO activities in Bosnia has been successful," Axworthy said in a statement. "Nevertheless, more work must be done before a durable peace can take hold."
The current Canadian contingent is with the Implementation Force (IFOR), led by the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. It is 50,000 to 60,000 strong.
The 1,200 Canadians would join the proposed NATO-led follow-on Stabilization Force that is to number 30,000.
